title: West Goshen drafts licensing rules for short-term rentals
summary: Proposed rules would require short-term rental hosts to get an annual license and inspection, file floor plans and parking details, and keep a guest register, with one off-street space per bedroom and $250-a-day fines for violations. Supervisors plan to vote Oct. 20.

title: Patchy West Union Street repaving prompts a look at utility-cut rules
summary: After PECO work left West Union Street only partly repaved, the borough's public works director explained that utilities patch just the trench above their lines. The borough is weighing ordinance changes to require more.

title: First NAMIWalks for Chester County set for Boot Road Park Oct. 3
summary: NAMI Chester County is holding its first NAMIWalks on Oct. 3 at 2 p.m. at Boot Road Park. Walking is free, and donations fund the group's local mental health programs.

title: WCU and Cheyney join a statewide push to bus students to college visits
summary: West Chester and Cheyney universities are part of the first outreach effort coordinated across all 10 State System schools, with the PASSHE Foundation covering transportation. The eastern Pennsylvania leg runs Nov. 2-10.

title: QVC Group starts over in West Chester after shedding $5 billion in debt
summary: The Wilson Drive shopping network left Chapter 11 on Aug. 6 with its long-term debt cut from $6.6 billion to $1.3 billion, a new $600 million lending facility and a Nasdaq listing under QVCG. Former chief Mike George has returned as board chairman and interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent leader.

title: Borough signs off on West Chester University's campus master plan
summary: Council approved the university's 800-page master plan with conditions after more than a year of negotiation over student housing, parking and public-realm changes. The plan sets the framework borough officials will measure future campus projects against.

title: Draft 2027 budget swaps the repealed stormwater fee for a tax increase
summary: Borough staff presented a 2027 budget Tuesday, Sept. 15 that raises property taxes to replace the roughly $1.2 million a year lost when the Stream Protection Fee was repealed. Borough Manager Sean Mettrick put the typical household's current tax-and-fee bill near $2,200, and the borough posted an online tool for comparing the old fee with the proposed tax.

title: East Bradford sets Oct. 1 hearing on a broad package of code changes
summary: Supervisors re-advertised the ordinance after a Sept. 10 hearing fell through and will now take it up at 6:30 p.m. Oct. 1. It would tighten door-to-door solicitation licensing, expand curb and sidewalk upkeep duties, ban overnight parking in township parks and allow sheds up to 500 square feet on some vacant residential lots.

title: Chester County History Center names Kim Collison its next president
summary: The High Street institution's trustees picked Collison, most recently Curator of Exhibitions at Winterthur Museum, to lead it starting Monday, Sept. 21. She spent a decade at Winterthur and guided its 2023 Ann Lowe: American Couturier show, the largest display to date of the trailblazing Black designer's gowns.

title: West Chester starts enforcing its 35-gallon trash can limit after Sept. 30
summary: The borough's updated garbage ordinance caps curbside trash cans at 35 gallons, and Public Works says larger cans will stop being collected once a grace period ends Sept. 30, with fines possible after that. The borough says it has no approved alternative for households that need bigger containers.
